description:
AVI HORIZONS es una iniciativa de AVI CONNECTION que investiga cómo mejorar la rapidez, seguridad y autonomía de la exploración espacial.

Soy Juan Gustavo Vargas Lara, estudiante de Ingeniería de Sistemas de la Universidad Continental. Participaré individualmente en NASA Space Apps 2026 desarrollando un simulador de misiones con programación, análisis de datos e IA.

Me interesan la astrofísica y la colaboración científica; valoro aportes en software, simulación y diseño.
summary:
AVI HORIZONS: Echoes of Time is an educational game in which students design and carry out a simulated Mars mission. Players choose instruments and a trajectory, manage limited spacecraft resources, respond to an onboard failure, land on Mars, and decide which scientific evidence to send to Earth.

The Faro 7 demo uses two historical Earth–Mars distances published by NASA/JPL to calculate communication delays. Players can replay the same scenario and compare whether waiting for Earth’s guidance or reconstructing a signal on board lets them recover and transmit the evidence in time. The mission log records each outcome, helping students see how engineering choices and communication delays affect what a mission can accomplish.
details:
AVI HORIZONS: Echoes of Time is a browser game that lets students plan and carry out a simulated Mars mission. Players select scientific instruments and a trajectory, balance spacecraft mass, power, and budget, respond to an onboard failure, and explore Mars with a rover. Their choices determine what evidence reaches Earth, and the mission log lets them compare outcomes.

In the Faro 7 demo, players have a 12-minute simulated window to recover an archive. They can wait for guidance from Earth or reconstruct the archive on board with Alex. The game uses two historical Earth–Mars distances published by NASA/JPL to calculate round-trip light travel time, then adds two simulated minutes for mission control. Replaying the decision shows how a longer communication delay can change which evidence the crew recovers.

We built the game with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript and published it on GitHub Pages. Its goal is to help students understand mission-design trade-offs by making decisions and seeing their consequences.
